# Railwatch

> Railwatch is a Ruby gem (the agent) that instruments a Rails application end
> to end — requests, jobs, scheduled tasks, rake/runner commands, database
> queries and N+1s, exceptions, cache, mail, notifications, broadcasts,
> outgoing HTTP, Active Storage, view renders, RubyLLM calls, and logs — links
> every one of them into a single execution tree by `execution_id`/`trace_id`,
> and sends them from a background thread over HTTPS to a Railwatch server:
> Railwatch Cloud (the default), a self-hosted railwatch-rs, or the one the
> separate `railwatch-server` gem runs next to Puma for an embedded dashboard
> at `/railwatch`. It replaces a separate APM and a separate error tracker
> with one gem and one configuration block, costs under a millisecond of CPU
> per request, and never writes to the application's primary database.
> Install is `bundle add railwatch` followed by
> `bin/rails generate railwatch:install` (`--prompt-token`, `--url` for a
> self-hosted server, `--kamal-secrets`), which writes the initializer,
> mounts the engine for the browser beacon, adds a Kamal post-deploy hook and
> the Inertia browser client where the app has them, and wires the test
> matchers. `bin/rails railwatch:doctor` prints a ✓/✗ line for every piece.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): what Railwatch is, where telemetry goes (Cloud, self-hosted, railwatch-server), the install, and where each document fits.
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): the install and where its token comes from, embedded with the `railwatch-server` gem, moving from 0.x embedded mode, the three optional lines, and deploying under Kamal, Docker/Heroku/Render, or no deploy tool at all.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): every configuration option and its `RAILWATCH_*` environment variable, plus the full public facade, redaction, rejection, transport and buffering behaviour, the dashboard gate railwatch-server uses, and the rake tasks.
- [Record types](docs/records.md): every record type the gem ships and every attribute on it, including RubyLLM calls (tokens, cost, finish reason, tool calls, workflows), sourced from the code that builds it.
- [Testing](docs/testing.md): the RSpec and Minitest matchers (`have_railwatch_queries`, `have_railwatch_n_plus_one`, `record_railwatch_span`, `record_railwatch_exception`, `have_railwatch_outgoing_requests`, `have_railwatch_http_in_transaction`) and a CI performance-gate recipe.
- [Production source maps](docs/source-maps.md): hidden Vite maps, private upload before publishing assets, safe opt-in deletion, resolved browser stacks and default issue grouping.
- [AI assistants and MCP](docs/ai-and-mcp.md): the server's MCP endpoint, how to get a token, paste-ready client configuration for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, and Zed, and every tool, prompt, and resource the server exposes.
- [Replacing Sentry](docs/replacing-sentry.md): a step-by-step migration — removing the gems, porting each option, rewriting each call site, breadcrumbs, spans, profiling, attachments, `before_send`, fingerprints, and release health.
- [Coming from Laravel Nightwatch](docs/replacing-nightwatch.md): the record-type mapping, what "execution" means in Railwatch, sampling parity, and the facade method names in Ruby.
- [Self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md): pointing the gem at a self-hosted railwatch-rs, creating a token there, and checking the connection.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): every `railwatch:doctor` line and the failure modes behind them — no records, doubled scheduled tasks, WebMock in specs, Puma fork, tail-sampling memory, missing profiler, missing deploy marker, Kamal hook, log search, empty tenants.
- [Security](docs/security.md): transport, capture defaults, the browser beacon, token handling, and application responsibilities.
- [FAQ](docs/faq.md): overhead numbers and how they are measured, retention, what is redacted by default versus opt-in, SQLite, and what happens when the platform is unreachable.

## For coding agents

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): how to install and use Railwatch from inside a Rails app — the facade methods, the spec matchers, `railwatch:doctor`, and the MCP hookup.

## Optional

- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md): released versions and what changed in each.
